clahe — 2D gray op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "clahe", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

▸ clahe: other inputs (docs site)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (tiled, bilinearly blended).

• a — number of tiles nb = 2 + int(3a) (the image is split into nb×nb)

• b — clip limit. Given as the factor 256**b relative to the mean count per bin (b=0 → 1 times = a completely flattened histogram = a straight tone map = zero enhancement; b=1 → 256 times = the maximum 1 bin can take, so clipping has no effect = plain AHE; b=0.5 → 16 times. OpenCV's default clipLimit=40 is roughly b=0.665).

★2026-09-02 (this fix): until then b was completely dead (measured:

max|clahe(x,0.5,0.0) - clahe(x,0.5,1.0)| == 0.0 exactly). The "C" in CLAHE is the C of contrast limited, and the clip limit is precisely what separates AHE from CLAHE, so the implementation was AHE, not CLAHE — the name was lying. Here the clip limit was implemented and assigned to b, and the factor was chosen so that b=1 is the end that is bit-identical to the old implementation (the upper limit at which no clipping occurs = 256 times, the number of bins).

Tiles PARTITION the image (linspace boundaries, so the last tile absorbs the H % nb / W % nb remainder), each tile's clip-limited CDF is its local tone map, and every pixel blends the maps of its (up to) 4 nearest tile centres with bilinear weights — the standard CLAHE interpolation (Zuiderveld 1994).

2026-08-30: interpolation added (KNOWN_ISSUES #4 — the old implementation flattened each tile independently, which produced discontinuities at tile boundaries (a grid visible to the naked eye)). In the neighbourhood of a tile centre that tile's CDF still dominates as is, so this is a continuous version of the same family of mappings as the old implementation.
